sources.citation: Johnson, Eric C. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 7: Defi language area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-019. Dallas: SIL International. 41 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Purely sociolinguistic (RTT comprehension of Gun, vitality, attitudes, lexical-similarity appendix for Phla-Phera varieties). No phonology; no mention of tone or stress; 'accent' refers only to three regional accents (southern/northern/western villages). States (sec. 2.1, p.2) 'Neither the Ethnologue (Grimes 1996) nor Capo (1986) mention Defi' and (App. C, p.16) 'Defi was not included among the Gbe word lists collected'.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo: Gbe language family overview. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-012. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification / macrolanguage discussion; lists Defi among five surveyed varieties 'not included in Capo's (1986:101) internal classification of Gbe'. No tone or stress statement.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2007. The Gbe language continuum of West Africa: a synchronic typological approach to prioritizing in-depth sociolinguistic research on literature extensibility. Language Documentation & Conservation 1(2):182-215. hdl:10125/1714
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress (only 'Kruskal's stress' of MDS plots). Table 1 reproduces Capo (1991:15) classification of 49 Gbe varieties; Defi is not among them, confirming Capo's Comparative Phonology of Gbe does not treat Defi.
